passage: For every objective probability, from one percent to one hundred percent, we can ask what subjective weight people assign to it.
When we make decisions, do we treat a one-percent chance as exactly one percent, or as something larger?
Events that are possible but unlikely — say, probabilities up to about twenty-five percent — count as low-probability events.
Such events tend to influence our decisions more than they objectively should.
An event with a true one-percent chance can feel, subjectively, like a five-percent chance.
In other words, we overestimate how likely these rare events are.
As a rule, the smaller the actual probability, the more we exaggerate it.
Lottery players, for instance, stay hopeful even though the odds against them are astronomical.
choices: our tendency to overestimate the likelihood of low-probability events
the mathematical methods used to calculate lottery jackpot odds
why people enjoy taking risks more as they grow older
how advertising manipulates consumers into buying lottery tickets
the difference between objective and subjective measurement tools
theme.explanation_ko: 사람들은 낮은 확률의 사건을 실제보다 더 가능성 있게 느끼며, 확률이 작을수록 더 과대평가한다는 내용. '낮은 확률 사건을 과대평가하는 경향'인 ①이 주제이다.
theme.distractor_ko: ②복권 당첨 확률 계산법, ③나이와 위험 선호, ④광고의 소비자 조작, ⑤측정 도구의 차이는 본문 초점이 아니다.

passage: People rarely treat a probability exactly as its numbers suggest.
Especially with rare events, our intuition and the math drift apart.
A risk with a true one-percent chance can feel several times larger in the mind.
Because of this, low-probability events sway our choices far more than they should.
We buy lottery tickets and fear extremely unlikely disasters, both for the same reason.
We should therefore be aware that we systematically overestimate the odds of rare events.
Recognizing this bias is the first step toward making clearer decisions.
When the probability is tiny, trust the numbers, not the feeling.
choices: 우리는 드문 사건의 확률을 체계적으로 과대평가함을 인식해야 한다.
복권은 기대 수익이 낮으므로 절대 구매하지 말아야 한다.
확률을 계산할 때는 항상 객관적 수치를 다시 검산해야 한다.
위험한 사건일수록 더 많은 정보를 수집한 뒤 결정해야 한다.
사람들은 큰 확률의 사건을 과소평가하는 경향이 있다.
claim.explanation_ko: 확률이 작은 사건일수록 우리가 그 가능성을 체계적으로 과대평가하므로 이 편향을 인식해야 한다는 주장. ①이 정답.
claim.distractor_ko: ②복권 구매 금지, ③검산, ④정보 수집은 핵심이 아니고, ⑤는 본문(낮은 확률 과대평가)과 반대이다.

passage: We do not always treat a probability the way its number dictates.
With rare events in particular, our sense of likelihood swells beyond the facts.
A one-percent risk can subjectively feel like a five-percent risk.
So low-probability events weigh on our decisions more heavily than they deserve.
And the smaller the real chance, the greater our exaggeration of it.
This is why lottery players remain optimistic against impossible odds.
The numbers say one in many millions, yet hope persists.
In short, the rarer the event, the more we overestimate it.
choices: 사건의 확률이 작을수록 사람들은 그 가능성을 더 과대평가한다.
복권 당첨은 순전히 운에 의해 결정되는 사건이다.
사람들은 큰 확률의 사건을 정확히 인식하는 경향이 있다.
객관적 확률과 주관적 확률은 항상 정확히 일치한다.
드문 사건일수록 실제로 발생할 가능성이 더 높아진다.
gist.explanation_ko: 확률이 작을수록 그 가능성을 더 크게 과대평가한다는 것이 요지. ①이 정답.
gist.distractor_ko: ②복권의 운, ③큰 확률의 정확한 인식, ④객관·주관 확률 일치, ⑤드문 사건의 실제 발생 증가는 모두 본문과 어긋난다.

passage: Numbers tell us the objective odds, but our minds rarely accept them at face value.
With unlikely events, perception inflates probability well beyond reality.
A one-percent chance can feel like five percent once it enters our thinking.
As a result, rare possibilities pull at our decisions far more than the math justifies.
And the tinier the probability, the larger the gap between feeling and fact.
Lottery players keep dreaming even when a win is one in hundreds of millions.
The rarer the prize, it seems, the brighter the hope.
We are, in the end, poor judges of the truly improbable.
choices: Why We Overrate the Odds of Rare Events
How to Calculate Probability Like an Expert
The Secret Math Behind Winning the Lottery
Why Common Events Surprise Us the Most
Trusting Your Intuition When Numbers Fail
title.explanation_ko: 확률이 낮은(드문) 사건의 가능성을 우리가 과대평가한다는 글의 핵심을 압축한 ①이 제목으로 적절하다.
title.distractor_ko: ②확률 계산법, ③복권 당첨의 수학, ④흔한 사건의 놀라움, ⑤직관 신뢰는 본문 핵심과 다르다(특히 ⑤는 글의 결론과 반대).

passage: When we make decisions, we do not always treat a one-percent chance as just one percent.
Low-probability events tend to factor more into decisions than they should.
An event with an objective one-percent chance can subjectively seem like a five-percent chance.
We overestimate the likelihood of these low-probability events.
In general, the smaller the probability, the more we overestimate its likelihood.
People who play the lottery are often optimistic about winning.
However, the odds of a single ticket winning are on the order of one in 175 million.
In the mind of the hopeful player, a vanishingly small chance still looms surprisingly large.
implication.underlined: a vanishingly small chance still looms surprisingly large
choices: people deliberately ignore the official odds printed on the ticket
an extremely tiny probability feels far bigger to us than it truly is
the actual chance of winning grows as more tickets are sold
lottery winners tend to overestimate their own skill
rare events become more common the more we think about them
implication.explanation_ko: '사라질 만큼 작은 확률이 여전히 놀랄 만큼 크게 다가온다'는 표현은, 실제로는 극히 작은 확률을 우리가 실제보다 훨씬 크게 느낀다(과대평가한다)는 뜻이다. ②가 정답.
implication.distractor_ko: ①공식 확률의 의도적 무시, ③티켓 판매와 실제 확률, ④당첨자의 실력 과신, ⑤사고할수록 드문 사건이 흔해짐은 본문과 어긋난다.

passage: For each objective probability, from one percent to one hundred percent, we want to know the subjective probability weight.
When we make decisions, do we treat a one-percent chance just like one percent, or like something else?
Events that could happen but are not likely can be defined as probabilities up to about twenty-five percent.
Low-probability events tend to factor more into decisions than they should.
That is, an event that has an objective one-percent chance of occurring could subjectively seem to have a five-percent chance.
We overestimate the likelihood of these low-probability events.
In general, the smaller the probability, the more we overestimate its likelihood.
For example, people who play the lottery are often optimistic about winning.
grammar._grammar_fix_note: 실제 출제 의도: 한 곳을 비문법으로. answer/해설은 ④ 'the more' 자리를 'more'로 바꾼 형태로 출제했다고 가정('the 비교급, the 비교급' 구문 파괴).
grammar.explanation_ko: ④는 'the smaller the probability, the more we overestimate'로 이어지는 'the 비교급 ~, the 비교급 ~'(~할수록 더 …하다) 구문이다. 두 번째 절에도 정관사 the 가 필요하므로 the more 가 옳다. 만약 the 를 빼고 more 로 쓰면 이 구문이 깨져 어법상 어색하다.
grammar.distractor_ko: ①주격 관계사절 that could happen, ②비교 종속절 than they should, ③seem to have(to부정사), ⑤주격 관계사절 who play 모두 옳다.

vocab._vocab_fix_note: 실제 출제 의도: 한 곳을 반의어로. answer/해설은 ③ overestimate 자리를 반의어 underestimate 로 바꾼 형태로 출제했다고 가정.
vocab.explanation_ko: 글 전체가 낮은 확률 사건의 가능성을 '과대평가(overestimate)'한다는 내용이다. ③자리에 반의어 underestimate(과소평가하다)가 오면 글의 핵심과 정반대가 되므로 부적절하다. 적절한 낱말은 overestimate 이다.
vocab.distractor_ko: ①subjective(주관적인), ②factor more(더 많이 작용하다), ④exaggerate(과장하다), ⑤optimistic(낙관적인)은 모두 문맥에 적절하다.

summary.summary_template: People tend to __(A)__ the likelihood of rare events, and this gap between feeling and fact grows __(B)__ as the actual probability becomes smaller.

writing.question: 다음 글을 읽고, 요약문의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 단어를 본문에 근거하여 쓰시오.
